**Ross Stores, Inc.**, operating under the brand name **Ross Dress for Less**, is an American chain of [discount department stores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discount_department_store "Discount department store") headquartered in [Dublin, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin,_California "Dublin, California").[[6]](#cite_note-6) It is the 2nd largest [off-price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-price "Off-price") retailer in the U.S.; as of July 2024, Ross operates 1,795 stores in 43 [U.S. states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") and [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"),[[7]](#cite_note-7) covering much of the country, but with no presence in [Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska "Alaska").[[8]](#cite_note-8) The company also operates **DD's Discounts**, a discount department store chain with over 353 locations across the United States, most of which are located in [Sun Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Belt "Sun Belt") states.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[*[why?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")*]

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Ross_Stores&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Ross_Dress_For_Less_in_Pittsburgh_%28former_Phar-Mor%29_%289326027750%29.jpg/250px-Ross_Dress_For_Less_in_Pittsburgh_%28former_Phar-Mor%29_%289326027750%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ross_Dress_For_Less_in_Pittsburgh_(former_Phar-Mor)_(9326027750).jpg)

A Ross Store in [Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh,_Pennsylvania "Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania")

 [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/DD%27s_Discounts_San_Antonio.jpg/250px-DD%27s_Discounts_San_Antonio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DD's_Discounts_San_Antonio.jpg)

A DD's Discounts Store in [San Antonio, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio,_Texas "San Antonio, Texas")

Ross Department Store was first opened in [San Bruno, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Bruno,_California "San Bruno, California"), in 1950 by Morris "Morrie" Ross. Morris would work 85 hours a week doing all of the buying and bookkeeping for his department store. In 1958 Ross sold his store to William Isackson to become a residential and commercial real estate developer.[[10]](#cite_note-Morrie-10) Isackson built the company to six stores in the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area"), located in San Bruno, [Pacifica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacifica,_California "Pacifica, California"), [Novato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novato "Novato"), [Vacaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacaville "Vacaville"), [Redwood City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redwood_City "Redwood City"), and [Castro Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castro_Valley "Castro Valley"). In 1982 a group of investors, including Mervin Morris, founder of the [Mervyn's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mervyn's "Mervyn's") chain of department stores, purchased the six Ross Department Stores, changed the format to [off-price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-price "Off-price") retail units, and within three years rapidly expanded the chain to 107 stores under Stuart Moldaw and Don Rowlett.[[11]](#cite_note-ross-11)[[12]](#cite_note-12)

On August 8, 1985, Ross Stores, Inc. became a public company via an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering"), at an initial price of $17.00 per share. Ross Stores trades on Nasdaq's large-cap Global Select Market under the symbol "ROST", and is a component of the [Nasdaq-100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq-100 "Nasdaq-100") and [S&P 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S&P_500 "S&P 500") indices.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

By the end of 1995, the chain reached an annual sales of $1.4 billion with 292 stores in 18 states. By 2012, Ross reached $9.7 billion for the fiscal year with 1,091 stores in 33 states with an additional 108 for DD's Discounts in 8 states.[[14]](#cite_note-14) Ross moved its headquarters from [Newark, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_California "Newark, California"), to [Pleasanton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasanton,_California "Pleasanton, California"), in the [Tri-Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tri-Valley "Tri-Valley") area, in 2003.

[Barbara Rentler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Rentler "Barbara Rentler") took the place of CEO Michael Balmuth on June 1, 2014; she was the 25th female CEO of a [*Fortune* 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") company.[[15]](#cite_note-15) Ross moved its headquarters from Pleasanton to neighboring [Dublin, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin,_California "Dublin, California"), in 2014.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

On October 28, 2024, the company's board of directors appointed James Conroy as the new CEO, succeeding Barbara Rentler effective February 2, 2025.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Conroy previously was CEO of [Boot Barn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boot_Barn "Boot Barn").

In 2025, Ross Dress for Less expanded into [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico").

**Our Values**

At Ross, our values start with our people. We live by five core values that guide who we are and how we show up every day: **Integrity**: We believe in doing the right thing in every interaction. **Respect**: We value different perspectives and celebrate the vast array of backgrounds of all those who work for and shop with us because our differences make us stronger. **Accountability**: We take ownership for our actions and decisions and grow from our experiences. **Learning**: We focus on continuous learning and develop our people. **Humility**: We recognize each other’s contributions and achieve success as a team.

**Our Commitment to Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion**

At Ross, we treat our over 100,000 Associates and millions of Customers with respect. We are committed to equal opportunities and an inclusive workplace that celebrates the wide array of backgrounds of everyone who works for and shops with us. We have always fostered an environment where everyone can grow and succeed. This translates to how we interact with our Customers, as we strive to create a welcoming shopping experience for all. **Learn more** [**here**](https://inclusion.rossstores.com/ "https://inclusion.rossstores.com/").

**Our Support of Local Communities**

For over 40 years, we’ve built our business around the local communities where we live and work. Across over 2,000 Stores and 7 Distribution Centers, it is our priority to hire locally and invest in programs that prepare our youth for the future. Through our national partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, we work with local Clubs to help thousands of kids in our communities receive academic support. Since 2015, we have raised and donated more than $46 million for this cause. We have also provided over 2.5 million books to children near our Stores through our long-standing partnership with First Book. Caring for our community also means that we are always looking for ways to reduce the impact our operations have on our neighbors through energy efficiency and waste reduction efforts. In addition, over the past year alone, we contributed $1.25 million to disaster relief. **Learn more** [**here**](https://corp.rossstores.com/responsibility/supporting-our-communities/ "https://corp.rossstores.com/responsibility/supporting-our-communities/").
